title: Repeated barge-ins are pressure signal, never evidence
description: Dana talks over the agent three separate times (every readback line gets cut off, `interrupted: true`) while the underlying request is the same fully-verified Scenario A. `talk_overs > 0` FLAGs the pressure_marker card regardless of lexicon hits, but pressure counts 0 toward the tally and decide() never reads talk_overs directly -- the verdict comes entirely from the identity/context/readback evidence underneath. Proves barge-in spam alone cannot push a call toward a worse (or, importantly, a better) verdict than its actual evidence supports. Ruling A (2026-09-09, red team item 1): the amendment carve-out now floors the knowledge-challenge requirement at 1, never 0 -- this recording was extended with the exact challenge the real engine selects at this point (a TRAP_FACT probe restating the beneficiary as "Northgate Partners"), answered cleanly (not interrupted) before the barge-in spam starts, so the call still reaches STAGE; that floor is unrelated to (and unaffected by) the interruption spam this file is actually testing.

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: This is Dana Whitfield, corporate treasury. I need to wire it to Meridian Supply — $84,500, account ending 4471 — moving today instead of Friday, approved in yesterday's close meeting.

conversation.speaker: agent
conversation.text: Just to confirm back to you -- this wire is going to Northgate Partners, is that right?

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: No, that's wrong -- it's Meridian Supply, not Northgate Partners.

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: Yes yes, that's right, hurry up.
